body.statement: Under independent sampling and for certified tolerance \(\delta_N=o(\rho_N)\), the positive Fourier minimum-distance estimator satisfies \(D_H(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)=O_{\mathbb P}(\rho_N)\) and \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)=O_{\mathbb P}\{\rho_N^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\}\), uniformly over the model class. In the primary case \(n=2\), \(k=2\), \(m=1\), this is \((N/\log N)^{-3/16}\).
body.justification: A computable estimator turns the population frontier into a usable finite-sample guarantee in the same symmetric quotient geometry, without numerical differentiation at critical points.
body.gap: Acartürk et al. give finite-sample recovery for linear mixers, and Lyu--Fu control a derivative diagnostic for nonlinear ICA; neither handles bounded nonlinear causal decoders or quotient loss.
body.consumer: Implementations on periodic latent coordinates obtain a certified stopping rule and representation error radius from environment samples.

obligation.what_is_open: Propagation of the proved complete-law rate to the claimed full-class encoder rate.
obligation.obstruction: The estimator ranges over arbitrary certified models in the full class, so only the unresolved full inverse-modulus upper bound can convert its law error to representation error.
obligation.attempted: The fixed-bias normalization was corrected, observed-density smoothness was derived, Fourier bias and variance were bounded, finite Hellinger nets were constructed, and the minimum-distance law oracle inequality was proved.
obligation.partial_result: The corrected estimator has the proved uniform law guarantee \(D_H(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)=O_{\mathbb P}(\rho_N)\). The representation guarantee requires the unproved full-class implication \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\lesssim D_H^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\); it cannot be obtained from the radial result because the estimator ranges over the full model class. If the rigidity question is resolved affirmatively, direct substitution gives the displayed representation rate and, for \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\), \(\rho_N^{3/4}=(N/\log N)^{-3/16}\).
